channel.title: Newspin: latest timeline updates
channel.description: Newspin turns the biggest ongoing news stories in India, the US and around the world into clear, sourced timelines: what happened, when, and what comes next.

item.title: Rupee: Rupee slips back past 93 as Indian shares fall
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 · The rupee settled at 92.62 per dollar on Friday, PTI reports. On Monday it opened at 93.47, briefly strengthened to 92.43, then fell back to 92.85 in early trade. Forex traders told PTI that cheaper oil helped at first, but a firm US dollar and selling in Indian shares weighed on it. By 12:30 pm it had fallen to 93.08, the day's low, per Business Standard, as the Sensex dropped about 1.1% by midday. These are intraday levels; the closing rate may differ.

item.title: COP31 climate talks: COP31 ends with no main agreement
item.description: 22 Nov 2026 · The final text referred to the 2023 agreement on moving away from fossil fuels without naming them, and kept support for carbon capture, per AFP and ABC Australia. The EU said it could not accept a text with no reference to fossil fuels, Panama rejected it and the Marshall Islands withheld support, per UN News, so the main decision was not adopted. "I understand that there is no agreement on this text. For that reason, these decisions have not been adopted," Kurum said. ABC Australia says the summit ended 44 hours after its official close, the longest UN climate summit on record, and that Russia and Saudi Arabia backed leaving fossil fuels out. Bowen called the outcome "very disappointing". UN Secretary-General António Guterres said: "There may be no consensus in the negotiating room. There is no ambiguity in the science."

item.title: COP31 climate talks: India says it engaged constructively and regrets the lack of consensus
item.description: 22 Nov 2026 · Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav said India "engaged constructively" until the end and regretted that no consensus was reached, per PTI. "Energy transitions must be nationally determined, just and equitable, backed by finance, technology," he said, adding that past emissions by rich countries "have consumed a disproportionate share of the global carbon budget". India sided with developing countries pressing for more climate finance.

item.title: Ukraine talks: Russian strikes on Kyiv region hit an apartment block and a supermarket; Zelenskyy asks the US for Patriot missiles
item.description: 22 Nov 2026 · A Russian strike early on Sunday destroyed part of a five-storey apartment block in Dymer, north of Kyiv. At least three people were killed and four wounded, per AP and the Kyiv regional governor via Ukrinform, and about a dozen were still believed trapped. On Sunday evening a drone hit a supermarket in the Vyshneve area of Kyiv region, killing at least two people and injuring eight, the governor said, per the Kyiv Independent. He declared 23 November a day of mourning in the region. Zelenskyy said Russia launched about 2,700 attack drones, nearly 1,460 guided bombs and 165 missiles over the past week, and urged the US to approve delivery of Patriot air-defence missiles that partners have already paid for, per Al Jazeera. No new talks or prisoner exchange were reported.

item.title: Delhi air: Sunday's daily AQI 239, 'poor'; forecast warns of 'very poor' air later in the week
item.description: 22 Nov 2026, daily average · Delhi's average AQI for Sunday was 239, in the 'poor' band (201–300), down from 265 on Saturday, per CPCB figures reported by The Pioneer and Daily Jagran. Of 56 stations, 8 were 'very poor', 36 'poor' and 12 'moderate'; the worst were Uttam Nagar (332) and IGNOU Maidan Garhi (330). Daily Jagran reports that vehicles caused 38.6% of PM2.5 pollution on Sunday, the largest share. The air-quality early warning system expects 'poor' air from Monday to Wednesday, then 'poor' to 'very poor' for the six days after, as weaker winds disperse pollution less. No change to GRAP curbs was reported; Stage I and II stay.

item.title: West Asia & oil: Iran says two supertankers hit mines east of Hormuz; UKMTO reports a tanker 'incident with military forces'
item.description: 22 Nov 2026 · Iran's navy said on Sunday that two oil tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines east of the Strait of Hormuz, saying the ships had switched off their tracking systems and entered a 'forbidden' area, per Xinhua. The Revolutionary Guards (IRGC) navy separately said two supertankers exploded on 'unauthorized' routes north of Oman's Al Ghanam Island. The ships were not named and no one else has confirmed the incident. On Sunday evening UKMTO, the British agency that tracks shipping, said a tanker 'was involved in an incident with military forces in the Gulf of Oman', near Chabahar, and that investigations were under way, per Euronews. It gave no ship name or casualties. Euronews says the area is near the US blockade line, but it is not known whether this involved one of the Iranian tankers said to be ready to test the blockade. The IRGC also said it shot down a US MQ-1 drone east of the strait; the US has not commented.

item.title: West Asia & oil: Trump says he could resume strikes on Iran after the new year if talks fail
item.description: 21–22 Nov 2026 (US time) · In a Fox News interview, President Trump said he was inclined to resume strikes on Iran after the new year if talks fail, per Arab Times and Iran International. Asked about Iranian tankers testing the US blockade, he said: "I hope they do, they'll all be at the bottom of the sea like the rest of the navy," per Arab Times. Iran International quotes him as saying: "I'm going to make a deal that is going to be permanent." Indirect talks continue, with Qatar passing messages, Arab Times reports. Iran's parliament speaker said a state of 'neither war nor peace' cannot continue, and a deputy foreign minister said Iran is still talking to the US but is ready for any scenario, per Iran International. No decision to strike has been announced.

item.title: US midterms: Van Hollen claims growing support in his challenge to Schumer; Trump weighs in
item.description: 22 Nov 2026 (US time) · Senator Chris Van Hollen, who launched a challenge to Chuck Schumer for leader of the Senate Democrats on 12 November, told NBC's Meet the Press that more than 15 senators back him, per Newsweek and HNGN. Newsweek's count of public statements has at least 16 senators backing Schumer and 6 backing Van Hollen. The vote is a secret ballot on 1 December; 28 of 55 eligible senators-elect are needed to win. On Truth Social, President Trump wrote: "It is going to be very hard for me to work with Chuck Schumer should he become Senate Majority Leader."

item.title: COP31 climate talks: Talks run into overtime as fossil fuels vanish from the draft deal
item.description: 20–21 Nov 2026 · The summit ran past its scheduled close on Friday 20 November. An early draft of the main decision, released in the second week, repeated the 2023 COP28 pledge to transition away from fossil fuels, per Forbes and Al Jazeera. A shorter later draft removed every mention of coal, oil and gas, and dropped a $120 billion target for adaptation finance, money to help poorer countries cope with climate impacts, per AFP and Forbes. AFP reports Saudi Arabia resisted strong fossil-fuel language; Al Jazeera says Saudi Arabia and other big oil and gas producers objected. Panama's environment minister said: "We are being held hostage by the petroleum mafia," per Forbes. Late on Saturday Kurum told delegates: "We believe that we have put forward a text which all the parties can agree upon."

item.title: Nvidia & Huang: New York Times also reports the SEC inquiry; questions over how Nvidia reports sales by region
item.description: 21 Nov 2026 (US time) · The New York Times reported on Saturday that the SEC is investigating Nvidia's accounting, citing people briefed on the confidential inquiry, per AFP. AFP says the inquiry is at an early stage and could end without charges, and that it is unclear whether it concerns a change in how Nvidia reports sales by region or the Huang affair. Last year Nvidia stopped reporting regional sales by customers' billing address and began using where customers are headquartered, which removed Singapore from the breakdown; Nvidia said this better reflects its revenue, per Reuters. The Financial Times had reported that Singapore made up almost half of global revenue before the change, Reuters says. Nvidia did not respond and the SEC declined to comment. Nvidia shares fell more than 20% over the week, per AFP. Separately, President Trump said: "I would love to see Jensen be given a second chance"; the board chair has ruled out Huang's return.

item.title: AI this week: Lean and Mathlib communities certify the computer-checked Riemann proof; human review still to come
item.description: 21 Nov 2026 · The communities behind Lean, a computer system that checks mathematical proofs, and its main maths library Mathlib issued a joint statement saying the formal proof correctly states and proves the Riemann Hypothesis, per Unite.ai and Kingy AI. Dozens of people rebuilt the proof, and independent checking programs accepted it; one MIT mathematician reported that all 175,187 modules compiled with no errors. The statement covers only the computer-checked proof. There is no human-readable paper yet, and mathematicians still have to understand why the proof works; Terence Tao said digesting it 'will take some time'. The Clay Mathematics Institute still lists the problem as unsolved: its $1 million prize requires publication, two years and broad acceptance.

item.title: Nvidia & Huang: California's attorney general says his inquiry covers civil and criminal state law
item.description: 20 Nov 2026 (US time) · A day after his office subpoenaed Nvidia, California Attorney General Rob Bonta said the inquiry looks at whether Nvidia or former CEO Jensen Huang gave the public false information about chip sales to China. He said state laws that ban misleading investors and the public include "both civil and criminal clauses", per Zhitong via Longbridge. Bonta said the inquiry is at a preliminary stage and no conclusions have been reached. An inquiry is not a finding of wrongdoing. Neither report includes a response from Nvidia.

item.title: AI this week: Trump threatens a 'tremendous tax' on US firms that build AI data centres abroad
item.description: 20 Nov 2026 (US time) · President Trump told reporters at the White House: "We're not going to allow companies to build data centers in other countries. If they do that, they can. But we're going to put a tremendous tax on them," per AP. He said he had not yet told his staff, and it was unclear how such a tax would work. No bill or order has been published. The largest tech firms may spend up to $1.8 trillion on AI next year, per UBS figures cited by AP. Data centres are the buildings full of computers that train and run AI models.

item.title: Outlook outage: Microsoft's final report: four problems at once caused the outage
item.description: 20 Nov 2026 · Microsoft published its final post-incident report to business customers on 20 November, replacing the preliminary one, per summaries by 365fanatic and AppleScoop. It says four things combined: a defect in a gateway update that had been rolling out since July, about 14% of gateway capacity being offline for routine maintenance, Teams traffic moving onto the gateway shared with Exchange Online email, and peak North American demand. At the worst point more than 80% of servers stopped responding, and the failure reached every region within about two hours. Load tests missed the bug because they ran on older machines with fewer processor cores. Microsoft found no malicious activity, said AI tools did not make the faulty change, and plans to give different services separate gateway capacity by early 2027.

item.title: Rupee: Forex reserves fall $14.2 billion to a three-month low; rupee on track for its best month in eight years
item.description: 20 Nov 2026 (week to 13 Nov) · India's foreign exchange reserves fell by $14.20 billion to $705.34 billion in the week to 13 November, the lowest in about three months, RBI data released on Friday show, per The Tribune and Moody's via TradingView. Foreign currency assets fell $7.90 billion and gold holdings $6.18 billion. Forex reserves are the dollars, other currencies and gold the RBI holds, partly to steady the rupee. Separately, Business Standard reports the rupee is up 2.46% in November so far, on course for its best monthly gain in more than eight years, helped by nearly $13 billion of foreign investment.

item.title: COP31 climate talks: COP31 opens in Antalya
item.description: 9 Nov 2026 · The UN climate summit opened in Antalya, Türkiye, due to run until 20 November. Türkiye's environment minister Murat Kurum is COP31 President, and Australia's climate minister Chris Bowen leads the negotiations. UN News said nearly 200 countries were attending. UN climate chief Simon Stiell said at the opening: "Progress is nowhere near far enough or fair enough."

item.title: Delhi air: Sunday morning: AQI eases to 237, with five stations 'very poor'
item.description: 22 Nov 2026 · Delhi's average AQI was 237 at 9 am on Sunday, per CPCB data from its Sameer app reported by The Patriot. That is 'poor' (201–300), but better than recent days. Five of 54 stations were 'very poor' (above 300), down from 25 on Saturday; the worst was IGNOU-Maidan Garhi at 377, then Uttam Nagar at 340. IANS gave an early-morning average of 236. The minimum temperature was 11.8°C, per IMD. The ban on construction from 5 to 20 November was lifted on Friday, IANS reports; Stage I and II curbs remain. Forecasts cited by Outlook expect the air to stay 'poor' until at least Tuesday.

item.title: West Asia & oil: Bahrain says two people were hurt in Saturday's Iranian attack on an industrial plant
item.description: 22 Nov 2026 · Bahrain's Interior Ministry said two people were injured when Saturday's Iranian attack hit a civilian industrial plant and started a fire: a Bahraini citizen, who is stable, and a Pakistani resident, who is in a critical condition. Earlier official statements had said no one was hurt. Bahrain's Foreign Ministry said the site was 'a purely civilian industrial facility', rejected Iran's reasons for the attack and said it keeps the right to defend itself under the UN Charter. The Revolutionary Guards said they had targeted US Patriot air-defence radars at two bases in Bahrain; this has not been confirmed.

item.title: West Asia & oil: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say they shot down a US drone over Hormuz
item.description: 21 Nov 2026 · Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said on Saturday that its forces shot down a US MQ-9 drone over the Strait of Hormuz with a newly deployed air defence system, per Iranian state media cited by ANI and Middle East Eye. The IRGC called it the 58th MQ-9 brought down by Iranian forces. No US confirmation or denial had been reported. Al Jazeera, via Occasional Digest, reports that efforts to end the war remain stalled: Iran's foreign minister said its conditions must be met for the strait to reopen, and President Trump said Tehran wants a deal but not one he can accept.

item.title: West Asia & oil: Two tankers hit leaving Hormuz; Iran fires missiles and drones at US bases in Bahrain
item.description: 21 Nov 2026 · Early on Saturday two tankers leaving the Gulf were hit by unknown projectiles, one about 20 km north of Khasab in Oman and one about 31 km east of it, said UKMTO, the British agency that tracks shipping. One was hit in the stern and one in the engine room; no one was reported hurt. Iran's navy said a tanker caught fire after hitting a mine in a restricted zone east of the strait; it is not clear if this was one of the two. On Saturday night Iran launched drones and ballistic missiles at US bases in Bahrain, per Iranian media cited by Euronews. Bahrain said its air defences intercepted several attacks and a fire broke out at a civilian industrial site, with no injuries. The Revolutionary Guards (IRGC) said they hit two Patriot missile batteries and a radar; Bahrain and the US have not confirmed this. The US military denied a separate IRGC claim that Iran damaged a US F-16 jet on Friday. Iran's deputy foreign minister said more than 14 Iranian tankers are ready to sail through the US blockade to China, and warned of a 'fierce military response' if they are stopped.

item.title: US ground stop: White House cyber director removed after a string of outages
item.description: 19–20 Nov (US time) · Sean Cairncross, the White House National Cyber Director, has been removed from his post, after the FAA ground stop and other technology outages drew criticism, Fox News and The National Desk report. President Trump did not dispute that he was fired, saying: 'Because I didn't think that person was good enough.' Trump called the outages 'all separate events', and Secretary of State Marco Rubio said officials found 'zero evidence' linking them to each other or to hackers, per Fox News. Kirsten Davies, the Pentagon's chief information officer, is to take over. Cairncross said it was 'an honor to serve'. Trump also urged Congress to provide $50 billion for air traffic control upgrades.

item.title: US shutdown deadline: Iran war splits Democrats ahead of the 11 December deadline
item.description: 12–20 Nov 2026 · Some Democrats say they will not back another funding law unless it limits money for the war with Iran. Senator Chris Van Hollen, with Senators Duckworth, Sanders and Bennet, said any deal 'must include language that restricts the Trump Administration from using appropriated funds to continue his war against Iran', per CBS News. Others warn against a shutdown: Rep. Rosa DeLauro, the top Democrat on the House Appropriations Committee, favours a short extension to February and said Americans 'may not believe that shutting the government down ends the war'. Democratic leaders Hakeem Jeffries and Chuck Schumer have not set out their approach. The administration is considering a stopgap running through March, Roll Call reported, per the Government Shutdown Tracker. A funding law needs 60 votes in the Senate. A White House official said the economic pressure on Iran means the President has no 'need to conduct major combat operations'.

item.title: AI this week: Anthropic mathematician claims a Riemann Hypothesis proof made with Claude; not yet verified
item.description: 20 Nov 2026 (US time) · An Anthropic mathematician announced on Friday that he believes he and Claude, Anthropic's AI model, have produced a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, a 167-year-old unsolved problem about how prime numbers are spread out, and of a wider version called the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, per IBM Think and Interesting Engineering. The argument was released mainly as computer-checkable code in the Lean proof language, with a four-page explanation. He credited Claude with 'rapid progress during the final stages'. The claim has not been peer reviewed, and independent mathematicians have yet to verify it. Fields Medal winner James Maynard told IBM Think: 'If this fully checks out, it is clearly a historic milestone in mathematics', adding that checking the Lean verification 'will take some time'. The problem is one of the Clay Institute's seven $1 million Millennium Prize Problems; Clay requires peer-reviewed publication and two years of scrutiny, so it remains officially unsolved.

item.title: Google Gemini: Gemini for Mac can now use apps for you
item.description: 19 Nov 2026 (US time) · Google added 'computer use' to the Gemini desktop app for Mac. The AI agent can carry out tasks by opening Mac apps and websites in a background window, while the user watches a live preview and can pause it, stop it or approve actions before they happen. It is available first in English in the US and needs a Google AI Plus, Pro or Ultra subscription, TechCrunch reports. Google did not say when it will reach other countries or devices.

item.title: OpenAI: OpenAI says its models helped improve AMD chip designs
item.description: 18 Nov 2026 · OpenAI said its AI models rewrote parts of the circuit code for AMD graphics chip (GPU) designs and improved 'PPA' by up to 14% against already optimised designs. PPA stands for power, performance and area: how much energy a chip uses, how fast it runs and how much silicon it takes up. Some of the changes are in an AMD design that has already been sent for manufacturing, per OpenAI. OpenAI president Greg Brockman said the work gave 'roughly an additional year of progress' on AMD's chip in less than five months. The figures are OpenAI's; reports say AMD verified smaller, single-digit gains, but AMD's own statement was not found.

item.title: US shutdown deadline: Stopgap law keeps the government open to 11 December
item.description: 1–2 Sep 2026 · With the new budget year starting on 1 October, the House passed a stopgap funding law, known as a continuing resolution, 370–48 on 1 September, and President Trump signed it on 2 September. It keeps spending at last year's levels until 11 December. Harvard's federal relations office says the Senate had passed it 90–6 in August.

item.title: US shutdown deadline: Record 76-day Homeland Security shutdown ends, without ICE and CBP
item.description: 30 Apr 2026 · The House passed the Senate's DHS bill by voice vote on 30 April and President Trump signed it, ending a 76-day lapse that HSToday calls the longest agency shutdown in US history. The law funds 20 of DHS's 22 agencies, including TSA, FEMA, the Coast Guard and the Secret Service, to 30 September. ICE and CBP were left out, to be funded through a separate budget bill that Republicans can pass without Democratic votes.

item.title: US shutdown deadline: Trump orders TSA workers paid as screeners quit
item.description: 27 Mar 2026 · With airport screeners missing paychecks, President Trump signed an order on 27 March to pay TSA workers from funds in last year's One Big Beautiful Bill Act, per HSToday and Wikipedia. The same day the Senate approved a deal funding DHS except Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Customs and Border Protection (CBP), but House Speaker Mike Johnson refused a House vote on it. TSA's acting head told Congress of 'nearly $1 billion in delayed paychecks', per HSToday.

item.title: US shutdown deadline: Homeland Security shutdown begins
item.description: 14 Feb 2026 · DHS funding ran out at 12:01 am US Eastern time on 14 February after Democrats blocked a second two-week extension, amid disputes over immigration enforcement. The rest of the government stayed open. Airport security screeners at the Transportation Security Administration (TSA), the Coast Guard and other DHS staff had to keep working without pay.

item.title: US shutdown deadline: A four-day partial shutdown ends; Homeland Security split off
item.description: 31 Jan – 3 Feb 2026 · Funding for about half of the government lapsed at midnight on 30 January 2026, after Senate Democrats withdrew support for funding the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) over immigration enforcement. The Senate passed a $1.2 trillion package 71–29 that funded five spending bills to 30 September but gave DHS only a two-week extension. The House approved it 217–214 on 3 February, the shutdown's fourth day, and President Trump signed it that afternoon. The law guarantees back pay for furloughed workers.

item.title: US shutdown deadline: The longest full shutdown ends after 43 days
item.description: 1 Oct – 12 Nov 2025 · US government funding ran out on 1 October 2025 after Congress failed to agree a budget, mainly over whether to extend health insurance subsidies under the Affordable Care Act. Hundreds of thousands of federal workers were sent home without pay; the Government Shutdown Tracker puts the number at about 670,000 or more. About 13,000 air traffic controllers kept working unpaid, and on 7 November the FAA ordered flight cuts at 40 major airports. The Senate passed a deal 60–40 on 10 November and the House 222–209 on 12 November; President Trump signed it the same day. It funded most agencies only until 30 January 2026 and guaranteed back pay.

item.title: Delhi air: Saturday morning: AQI 278, with 25 stations 'very poor'
item.description: 21 Nov 2026 · Delhi's average AQI was 278 on Saturday morning, per official data reported by PTI, up from 269 on Friday morning. That is 'poor' (201–300). Twenty-five of 57 stations were 'very poor' (above 300), up from 14 on Friday; the worst was DTU at 369 at 9:05 am. The minimum temperature at Safdarjung was 12.2°C, slightly below normal and warmer than Friday's 10.5°C. Stage I and II curbs remain in force, per ETV Bharat. IMD expects winds to slow as it gets colder, which can trap pollution.

item.title: Ukraine talks: Kushner says Russia accepts Europe at the table; Moscow rejects any NATO-style role for Kyiv
item.description: 19–20 Nov 2026 · After the Berlin meeting of Ukraine's allies, US envoy Jared Kushner said: 'I think we've gotten the Russians comfortable with that concept where any security guarantee for Ukraine would be based on Article 5.' Article 5 is NATO's rule that an attack on one member is an attack on all. He also said Russia had agreed to talks that include Europe. Moscow has not confirmed this. Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov said any 'quasi membership' of NATO for Kyiv was 'totally unacceptable', and that a visit by European representatives was 'under consideration'. Zelenskyy said the next meeting would be four-way: Ukraine, the US, Russia and Europe. No date has been set.

item.title: Ukraine talks: Russia strikes three Kyiv bridges after Putin promises a response
item.description: 20 Nov 2026 · Overnight Russian ballistic missiles damaged the Podilskyi, Darnytskyi and Southern bridges over the Dnipro in Kyiv, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. Traffic was restricted and people crossed the river on foot. Prime Minister Koretskyi said eight people were killed, six of them in Kyiv, and 28 wounded. Russia's Defence Ministry said it targeted bridges used to move weapons, plus defence, energy and transport sites. Power was cut across Kyiv and in 10 regions after nuclear plants reduced output, Ukraine's energy ministry said. Putin had said in China: 'We will respond to these attacks.'

item.title: Ukraine talks: Russian strike on Kryvyi Rih, Zelenskyy's hometown, kills two
item.description: Night of 20 Nov 2026 · A Russian strike hit the centre of Kryvyi Rih on Friday night. A 7-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman were killed, the head of the city administration said. The regional military administration said 60 people were wounded, including six children. City officials said about 25 apartment buildings, a hospital and schools were damaged. Asked about Trump calling Putin his "friend", Zelenskyy told CNN that for Ukraine Putin is "an enemy". There is still no date for a new round of talks.

item.title: Nvidia & Huang: Reuters: SEC staff examining possible accounting issues at Nvidia; shares fall 14%
item.description: 20 Nov 2026 (US time) · Two people briefed on the matter told Reuters that enforcement staff at the SEC, the US markets regulator, are examining "potential accounting issues" at Nvidia. Reuters could not find out when the inquiry began or which issues it covers. The Wall Street Journal had reported an SEC probe on 17 November without saying what it focused on. The SEC declined to comment and Nvidia did not immediately respond, per Reuters. An inquiry is not a finding of wrongdoing, and many end without action. Nvidia shares closed down 14.01% at $125.53, per Yahoo Finance and CappNotes, the worst day since January 2025, per CappNotes. Reuters, citing LSEG data, says shares were already down more than 6% before its report.

item.title: Nvidia & Huang: Huang to testify in public before the Senate Banking Committee; no date set
item.description: 20 Nov 2026 (US time) · Jensen Huang has agreed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee, a spokesperson for its chairman, Senator Tim Scott, told Politico on 17 November. Scott told CNBC on 18 November that Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick had agreed to appear and that he hoped to hold the hearing "before Christmas". His letters had asked for Huang on 3 December and Lutnick on 10 December. On 20 November Scott's spokesperson confirmed the testimony will be public, CNBC reported, with no date set. Whether witnesses will testify under oath had not been decided, per Streamline. This is separate from Huang's closed-door interview with three House committees on 1 December.

item.title: AI this week: AI shares slide as Reuters reports SEC probe of Nvidia's accounting
item.description: 20 Nov 2026 (US time) · Reuters reported, citing two people briefed on the matter, that staff at the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) are examining possible accounting issues at Nvidia. Reuters could not say when the inquiry began or which practices are being reviewed. The SEC declined to comment. An investigation is not proof of wrongdoing. Nvidia's shares fell sharply, and the Motley Fool estimated about $491 billion of its market value was wiped out in a day. Anthropic's shares fell to within five cents of their $83 IPO price before closing at about $88 to $89 ($88.91 per Yahoo Finance and CappNotes, $88.30 per 24/7 Wall St).
